silabus_tekst: RNU study course “Business Management” description Study program Information Systems Amount 9 CP = 225 ac.h. Author (s) Viktoriia Riashchenko Preliminary knowledge, Related study courses Aim To provide in-depth knowledge in business processes, to promote the ability to use the acquired knowledge, skills and methods in practice and professional development, starting commercial activities and creating companies, as well as leading teamwork. Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) 1. Ability to develop in-depth knowledge of business processes, gaining professional competencies necessary for building and managing successful business ventures. 2. To acquire practical skills in organizing and founding companies, understanding the fundamentals of business management, and leading teams effectively. 3. To gain a solid understanding of the legal frameworks regulating labour relations, including corporate governance, labour law, and social dialogue within organizations and society. 4. Ability to learn to apply strategic management theories, such as corporate life cycles and organizational design, to real-world business challenges and decision-making processes. 5. To develop the ability to manage change within an organization, understanding the importance of strategic roles, effectiveness assessments, and the implementation of change strategies. 6. Ability to analyze an organization's internal resources, including financial and human capital, and apply performance management tools to ensure organizational success and sustainability. 7. Ability to enhance their competence in finding, evaluating, and structuring information, and will be able to clearly communicate this knowledge to others, improving decision-making and problem-solving skills. Literature and other sources of information: Compulsory reading - Jones G.R. (2013) Organizational Theory, Design, and Change, 7th ed.2013, Pearson, 512 p. - Tricker, B. (2019). Corporate Governance. Principles, Policies, and Practices. Oxford University Press, 568 p. Recommended - "Information Technology for Management: Driving Digital Transformation to Increase Local and Global Performance, Growth and Sustainability (2021) 12th Edition by Efraim Turban, Carol Pollard, Gregory Wood" - Adizes, I. (2015) Managing Corporate Lifecycles. Part II. Library of Congress Cataloging-in-Publication Data. Published by Adizes Institute Publications, 260 p. - Adizes I. K. (2018) Prasmīga pārmaiņu vadība. Ievads organizāciju terapijā. Zvaigzne ABC, 336 lpp. - Adizes, I.K (2016) Mastering Change - Introduction to Organizational Therapy (Revised Updated Edition). Adizes Institute Publications, 298 p. - Barney, J.B. Hesterly W.S. (2015) Strategic Management and Competitive Advantage. 5th ed., Pearson Education - Boddy, D. (2014). Management an introduction. New York: Pearson Education Limited. - Corporate Governance of State-Owned Enterprises A Toolkit (2014). The World Bank, 360 p. - Daft, R.L. (2014). Management. South-Western Cengage Learning - Daft, R. L. (2010) New Era of Management. Mason, OH, USA South- Western CENGAGE Learning. - Huczynsky A.A., Buchanan D. A. (2013) Organizational Behaviour, Eight edition, Pearson, Education, 760 p. - Lawrence J. Gitman, Chad J. Zutter (2012). Principles of Managerial Finance, Prentice Hall - Lester, D., Parnell, J. and Carraher, S. (2003). Organizational life cycle: A five-stage empirical scale. International Journal of Organizational Analysis, 11(4), p. 339-354 - Performance Management. Multidisciplinary Perspectives (2010) Ed. Thorpe R. Holloway J, University of Leads, UK Study course content and schedule of contact hours Week Topic Academic hours 1 Corporate Governance. Definitions. Content and topics of the course. Organization life cycle concepts. Stages of organization development. Characteristics of an organization at each stage of the life cycle. 8 2 Corporate development stages and managerial roles. Corporate Lifecycle by Adizes. Organization size and structural control. Control strategies. Weitzel and Jonsson's Model of Organizational Decline. Causes of decline. 8 3 Organizations and environment. Interface between organization and environment. General environmental factors and Task factors. Elements of a changing environment. Dimensions of uncertainty and organizational responses. Uncertainty and organizational structures: mechanistic and organic design. Strategic choices. 8 4 Organizational Design and Structure. Purpose of functioning of organizations. Factors affecting the functioning of an organization. Work system and organizational structure. Relation of structural approach to strategy. 8 5 Changes in the Company. Strategic Types of Change. The need for change. The strategic role of change. Elements of successful change. Model of the process of continuous change in organizational change. Barriers and resistance to change. Decision-making and decision-implementation processes. 8 6 Organizational Effectiveness. Assessing the effectiveness of an organization in a particular environment. Organizational effectiveness for sustainable growth. Measuring Organizational Effectiveness: external resource approach; internal systems approach; technical approach. Four dimensions of organizational effectiveness. Indicators of Organizational Effectiveness. Strategic constituencies' satisfaction: Stakeholders approach. 8 7 Assessment of the internal potential of the organization. Analysis of internal resources. Appraising resources. Organization Capabilities and Competencies. The company's value creation system management. Company's balanced evaluation by different capitals: financial, information, customer, human, social, relationship and intellectual capital. VRIO framework: a strategic internal analysis tool. 8 8 Organizational Performance and Performance Management. Measuring organizational performance. Performance control tools: financial control, information control; benchmarking, best practice approach. Balanced scorecard approach. Manager's role in helping organizations achieve high performance. Ethical dilemmas in corporate governance. Corporate Social Responsibility. 8 9 General provisions of labor law. 4 10 Social organizations of employees and employers. 4 11 Establishment of employment legal relationships and specifics of the employment relationships for individual categories of employees. 4 12 Peculiarities of working time determination. 4 13 General terms and conditions of remuneration. 4 14 Rest time. 4 15 Termination of employment. 4 16 Arrangements and time limits for dealing with industrial disputes. 4 Total: 96 ac.h Description of students’ self-studies organization and assignments Self-study work Description Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) % of final evaluation Students are required to study the indicated compulsory reading, sources, and methodological materials, as they are essential for understanding the fundamental concepts, completing assignments, and successfully mastering the course content. Detailed descriptions of each independent task and the assessment system are provided in the e-learning environment. Industry Case Studies Encourage students to delve into real-world case studies of companies that have successfully integrated technology and computer systems to achieve strategic outcomes. This may include an analysis of company practices, decision-making processes, and outcomes resulting from technology- driven initiatives. Critical Analysis - The ability to critically evaluate and analyze research on technology-based business initiatives in the real world, identifying key strategies and outcomes. Strategic Insight - Gain strategic insight into how technology can be effectively used in a business context, based on real-life examples. Decision-Making Skills - Improve decision-making skills by examining different business scenarios and technology implementations (PLO 1, 4, 6, 7). 20% Emerging technologies Encourage self-exploration of emerging technologies and their potential impact on business management. This may include exploring areas such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT) and their relevance to modern business operations. Technology Literacy - Developing an understanding of new technologies and their potential impact on business management and systems analysis. Innovative Thinking - Promoting innovative thinking by exploring the potential applications of cutting-edge technologies in business. Strategic Foresight - Developing the ability to anticipate the impact of new technologies on future business practices and strategies (PLO 1, 4, 5, 7). 20% Business Process Optimization Encouraging students to explore self-study materials that focus on process optimization methodologies and how they can be applied in a technology-driven business environment. This could include lean management, Six Sigma, and agile methodologies. Process Improvement Skills - Gaining skills in identifying and optimizing business processes in a technology- enabled environment. Analytical Capabilities - Improving analytical capabilities to evaluate business processes and implement improvements using technology solutions. Operational Efficiency - Understanding how technology can contribute to operational efficiency and effectiveness in business processes (PLO 1, 2, 5, 6). 15% Thought Leadership in Business and Technology Encouraging students to engage with thought leaders at the intersection of business and technology, including authors, industry experts, and influential figures who have shaped the conversation about the role of technology in business success. Idea Leadership Awareness - Building awareness of influential thought leaders and their contributions to building understanding of the role of technology in business success. Critical Analysis - Strengthening critical analysis skills by examining different perspectives and opinions in the business and technology environment. Thought Leadership Integration - Integrating idea leadership concepts and insights into technology- based business strategies and solutions (PLO 1, 4, 7). 15% Examination Comprehensive examination covering all course content. Synthesis of all acquired knowledge, skills, and competencies in business management and technology integration (PLO 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7). 30% Evaluation of mastering the study course Level Requirements Very high (10 –with distinction 9 – excellent) 10 (with distinction) - Knowledge, skills and competences exceed the requirements of the study course and demonstrate the ability to perform independent research as well as the deep understanding of problems. 9 (excellent) - Knowledge, skills and competences fully meet the requirements of the study course, student is able to apply the acquired knowledge independently. High (8 –very good 7 - good) 8 (very good) – The requirements of the study course are fully met, however, there is insufficient understanding of individual issues to use the knowledge independently for the solution of more complex problems. 7 (good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however, sometimes the inability to use the acquired knowledge independently is detected. Average (6 – almost good 5 – satisfactory 4 –almost satisfactory) 6 (almost good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however insufficient understanding of some problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 5 (satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met for the most part, however insufficient understanding of many problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 4 (almost satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met, for the most part, however insufficient understanding of some main concepts is detected as well as considerable difficulties in the practical application of the acquired knowledge are stated. Low (3 – 1 – negative evaluation) 3 (bad) – Knowledge is superficial and incomplete; the student is unable to use it in specific situations, 2 (very bad) – Superficial and incomplete knowledge of only some problems, the most part of the study course is not mastered. 1 (very very bad) – An absence of understanding of the main problems of the subject matter, almost no knowledge of the content of the study course.
